summary: In July 2025 Sindh's provincial ombudsperson for workplace harassment found K-Electric CEO Moonis Alvi had harassed a female employee and ordered his removal and a fine; Alvi denied the charges. The Sindh governor set the order aside on appeal in February 2026, and Alvi resigned days later, per a stock exchange disclosure. A challenge to the governor's decision is pending in the Sindh High Court.
note: Ombudsperson finding set aside by the governor; challenge pending in court.

He was removed from his position in 2015. The case drew wide attention in December 2020, when retailers pulled the brand's products.
note: Single source; judgment not found.

Disney gave no reason for his departure, and his representatives called the reports false and defamatory.
note: Single anonymous report; Disney gave no reason; he denied it.

summary: In 1997 the EEOC sued Sidney Frank Importing Co., the US importer of Jägermeister, alleging that more than 100 female employees were sexually harassed by its president and owner, Sidney Frank, and by other managers and customers. In June 1999 the company agreed to a federal consent decree in the Southern District of New York to pay $2.6 million into a claims fund, train supervisors, adopt an anti-harassment policy and drop mandatory arbitration of discrimination claims, the EEOC said. The EEOC release does not state whether the company admitted the allegations.

In September 2023 the company acknowledged the abuse, apologized, and said it would compensate victims, and its president resigned, AP and Bloomberg reported. Kitagawa, who died in 2019, was never charged and had denied the accusations while alive.

outcome: Convicted; 7-year prison sentence upheld by Supreme Court 2019
summary: The Seoul Central District Court in September 2018 convicted theatre director Lee Youn-taek of sexually assaulting and harassing eight actresses and staff members of his troupe on 25 occasions since 2010, finding they were under his influence, the Korea Times reported. The Seoul High Court raised his sentence to seven years and the Supreme Court upheld it in 2019. Lee had said the contact was acting guidance and consensual.

role: Music Director Emeritus; Artistic Director, Lindemann Young Artist Development Program
summary: The Metropolitan Opera said in March 2018 that an outside-counsel investigation found credible evidence that Levine had engaged in sexually abusive and harassing conduct before and during his Met tenure, including toward early-career artists under his authority. The Met ended its relationship with him after suspending him in December 2017. Levine had denied the allegations; no criminal charges were filed.

LA Opera said in March 2020 that a Gibson Dunn investigation found credible the accounts of 10 women who alleged inappropriate conduct by Domingo between 1986 and 2019. Investigators found no evidence of quid pro quo or retaliation. Domingo, who resigned as general director in October 2019 after AP reported the allegations, denied unwanted contact; he apologized after a union inquiry and later said the apology gave a false impression.

The Cleveland Orchestra fired concertmaster Preucil in October 2018 after a Debevoise & Plimpton investigation found he engaged in sexual misconduct and sexually harassing behavior with multiple female students and colleagues over years. The orchestra had suspended him in July 2018 after a Washington Post report. Preucil admitted sexual contact with three students but denied other misconduct.

role: Vice President, advertising and promotions, Fox News
outcome: EEOC suit settled for $225,000 (2006); Fox denied wrongdoing
summary: In November 2005 the EEOC sued Fox News Network on behalf of four women who alleged that a vice president in its advertising and promotions department, Joe Chillemi, created a sexually hostile workplace with obscene and derogatory remarks about women, and that one woman was retaliated against for complaining. In July 2006 Fox agreed to a consent decree paying $225,000 to the four women and requiring training and policy changes, the Associated Press reported. Fox denied the claims, and settlements are not admissions of wrongdoing.

category: Sexual harassment (public settlement with labour prosecutors)
summary: Pedro Guimarães resigned as president of state bank Caixa in June 2022 after Metrópoles reported sexual harassment allegations from employees. In April 2023 Caixa agreed with Brazil's labour prosecutors to pay R$10 million in collective moral damages over the harassment episodes, and a federal court accepted criminal charges against him in 2023; that case is pending. Metrópoles reported that a report by Caixa's internal affairs office corroborated the allegations. Guimarães denies the allegations, and his defence questioned the impartiality of the internal inquiry.

role: Director of Principal; deputy to the CEO of EDC (former director of Catalunya Ràdio)

summary: In November 2024 Barcelona Criminal Court No. 7 convicted Saül Gordillo, a former director of Catalunya Ràdio, of sexually assaulting a journalist at the digital outlet he directed, during a company Christmas dinner in December 2022. He was sentenced to one year in prison and two years of supervised release. The Barcelona Provincial Court upheld the conviction in February 2025, and Spain's Supreme Court rejected his appeal in May 2025. In September 2025 a second court approved a plea agreement over a complaint by another journalist about the same night, Ara reported.

category: Sexual harassment of a staff member
outcome: Dismissed from service and fined Rs1 million
summary: Pakistan's Federal Ombudsperson for Protection against Harassment of Women at Workplace found PTV general manager Khalid Mehmood Lakhan guilty of sexually harassing a makeup artist at PTV Centre Multan and ordered his dismissal and a Rs1 million fine, Dawn reported. President Arif Alvi rejected his representation and upheld the penalties in May 2023.
note: Ombudsperson finding upheld; as a regional station GM he is likely below VP level.

summary: Kenya's Employment and Labour Relations Court ruled in 2025 that ARTICLE 19's 2019 dismissal of Eastern Africa regional director Henry Maina for gross misconduct was lawful, finding sexual harassment through unwelcome suggestive messages to a female colleague proven, HapaKenya reported. The court rejected his argument that the messages were protected expression and dismissed his damages claims.
note: Labour court found harassment proven; judgment not located and only one outlet opened.

category: Indecent assault of a trainee employee
outcome: Convicted; 6 months suspended 2 years; removed from operations
summary: The Seoul Eastern District Court in April 2026 sentenced Next Kitchen CEO Jung Seung-bin to six months in prison, suspended for two years, for molesting a trainee employee, the Herald reported. Jung admitted the charge and reached a settlement with the employee. Next Kitchen had said in January 2026 that he would be excluded from operations, though he remained registered as its internal director.
note: Convicted and admitted it, but the company is small.

outcome: Convicted Sept 2025; 13 months' jail; appeal pending
summary: A Singapore district court convicted Hype Records executive director Ken Lim in September 2025 of molesting a 25-year-old woman during a work meeting at the label's office in 2021 and sentenced him to 13 months' jail, The Star reported. He has appealed the conviction.
note: Convicted, but the woman was a talent recruit, not an employee; appeal pending.

summary: The Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra ended its work with chief conductor Gatti in August 2018, citing reports of inappropriate behavior after a Washington Post article, and said the matter had irreparably damaged trust. Gatti had apologized to women he worked with, then through his lawyer firmly denied the allegations. The orchestra and Gatti later settled the dismissal dispute.
note: Orchestra's wording ('inappropriate behaviour') does not name sexual conduct; dismissal dispute later settled.

summary: Emerson Collective said in October 2017 it ended its business relationship with Wieseltier after learning of past inappropriate workplace conduct, and suspended the magazine he was to edit. Wieseltier apologized for offenses against some of his colleagues in the past. The New York Times reported that women who worked with him at The New Republic described harassment and unwanted advances.
note: Employer cited 'inappropriate workplace conduct' without naming sexual conduct.

role: Senior Creative Director, World of Warcraft
summary: Activision Blizzard said in 2021 that it had investigated former World of Warcraft creative director Afrasiabi and terminated him in 2020 for misconduct in his treatment of other employees. California's civil-rights lawsuit against the company alleged he made unwanted advances toward female employees at BlizzCon 2013. He did not publicly respond.
note: Company confirmed misconduct firing; seniority and sexual element in the company's own words unconfirmed.

summary: Actor Terry Crews, who identified himself publicly, sued Venit and WME alleging Venit groped him at a 2016 party. WME suspended Venit and removed him as head of its motion picture group, and in September 2018 said the parties had settled the lawsuit; Venit retired from the agency. Settlements are not admissions, and prosecutors declined to charge, citing the statute of limitations.
note: Settled, but the complainant was a client, not a colleague.

note: Only NYT originated; Hearst announced resignation. Unchanged.

summary: In October 2014 a federal jury in Dallas found for the EEOC in a suit alleging that Jim McKinney, CEO of EmCare's AnesthesiaCare division, sexually harassed a subordinate. The jury awarded $250,000 in punitive damages to that employee. It also found that EmCare fired two other employees in retaliation for complaining about the sexually hostile environment. The Fifth Circuit affirmed the retaliation verdict in May 2017 (857 F.3d 678).

summary: A Los Angeles jury found AT&T Information Systems liable for sexual harassment and retaliation against an area personnel manager, awarding $1.5 million in compensatory and $500,000 in punitive damages. The California Court of Appeal affirmed the verdict in 1993 (13 Cal.App.4th 976). The opinion describes the harasser as area vice-president Peter Fellows and says company supervisors had received earlier reports about his conduct. According to the opinion, Fellows had resigned by then.

The company said an inquiry led by its corporate auditors with outside experts found the report to be true, and that its nomination committee had concluded the conduct warranted a resignation recommendation as director and dismissal as executive officer. Kureha withheld his bonus and forfeited part of his stock compensation; the president and other directors returned part of their pay.

Weißmann rejects any misconduct and is pursuing legal steps; the employee disputes the review's findings.

summary: The Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal suspended Timothy Eagle, former senior partner at Norwich firm Hansells, from practice for 12 months in February 2026 and ordered £30,000 in costs. The tribunal found that at a December 2022 office Christmas gathering he made sexually explicit comments to several female colleagues and engaged in unwanted physical contact. Eagle admitted all four allegations but denied a lack of integrity and denied that one remark was sexually motivated. He self-reported to the regulator, and the firm suspended him; he retired before its internal process ended.

summary: Honolulu Civil Beat reported that the Rehabilitation Hospital of the Pacific removed Dr. Jason Chang as chief medical officer in June 2019, after two employees complained. An outside investigator hired by the hospital concluded that the sexual activity with a subordinate was more likely than not unwelcome. Chang admitted an inappropriate sexual relationship with a subordinate on hospital grounds but maintained it was consensual and denied harassment. A federal judge denied his request to stop the hospital reporting him to the National Practitioner Data Bank.

outcome: Terminated; court later held firing was not for cause

A Massachusetts trial court found the firing was not for cause under his stockholders' agreement, and the Supreme Judicial Court affirmed in Balles v. Babcock Power (2017). The courts found that he violated company policies but held that the agreement's notice-and-cure requirements were not met.

summary: TVF founder Arunabh Kumar stepped down as CEO in June 2017 after several women, including a former employee, accused him of sexual harassment, and Mumbai police registered cases. TVF had initially called the allegations false; Kumar later apologised for that response.

summary: Hernando José Gómez resigned as president of Colombia's banking association Asobancaria in November 2022. El Espectador reported that the complaint alleged sexual harassment of a subordinate; Gómez acknowledged a brief kiss, which he described as a spontaneous greeting, denied using force and denied that his conduct was harassment. Colombian prosecutors closed the criminal file in March 2023 and later reopened it.

Metrópoles later reported that a confidential Globo compliance document concluded he had harassed former subordinates and breached its code of conduct. Melhem denies the allegations; Brazilian outlets report a criminal harassment case was later closed through a plea arrangement (transação penal) with Rio prosecutors, which is not a conviction.
